propositions: The autouse _no_repo_commits guard invokes git rev-parse HEAD before and after every test, creating ~26k subprocess calls across the 13,255-test suite with measured 7.826ms per call on macOS, projecting 207.4 runner-seconds overhead.

Eliminating per-test Git subprocesses via in-process HEAD fingerprinting after one-time per-worker worktree discovery would preserve per-test checkout attribution, the allow_repo_writes escape hatch, and the session dirty-tree backstop.

A-B-B-A measurements on 895 tests showed 9.3% median wall-time savings (5.04s, projecting ~75s at full suite) when the guard was bypassed, but no fidelity-preserving implementation reached consensus approval: adding a Git library expands dependency risk, hand-parsing refs is unsafe, and removing attribution weakens coverage.

Four major active OSS projects (pytest, pip, Poetry, pre-commit) are 4/4 consensus against per-test source-checkout Git subprocesses, but none maintains rebar's stronger per-test attribution contract or implements a consensus fidelity-preserving primitive.
No implementation option was automatically approved; the ticket was moved to blocked pending explicit operator design choice or new evidence for a safe primitive.
